title: The Salt Path Home
author: Marguerite Ellery
description: A family returns to the coastal town they swore they had left for good; Ellery writes tides the way others write memory.

title: The Cartographer’s Daughter
author: Marguerite Ellery
description: A girl inherits her father’s unfinished atlas and spends a decade deciding whether to complete it.

title: Weatherhouse
author: Marguerite Ellery
description: Three generations of women keep a lighthouse that has not been lit in forty years.

title: A Grammar of Silence
author: Yusuf Karim
description: A translator loses the ability to speak and begins a notebook of everything she cannot say.

title: The Quiet Instrument
author: Hélène Marceau
description: A luthier takes a final commission from a client who will not explain what the instrument is for.

title: Bright Interval
author: Hélène Marceau
description: Two strangers share a train compartment across a country neither of them can name.

title: The Wintering
author: Ada Fenwick
description: A novel about the year a village agreed, without discussing it, to stop speaking to one another.

title: Small Mercies of the Tide
author: Ada Fenwick
description: Fenwick’s breakthrough: a fishing town, a drowned boy, and forty years of careful silence.

author: Josiah Bell

title: Nine Kinds of Leaving
author: Josiah Bell

title: The Orchard at Dusk
author: Priya Anand
description: An inheritance dispute over an orchard becomes an argument about what a family owes its dead.

title: Paper Cities
author: Priya Anand

title: The Long Sunday
author: Tomas Bergqvist
description: One day in a small Swedish town, told sixteen times from sixteen windows.

title: Harbour Light
author: Nuala Devine
description: A harbourmaster’s logbook becomes an accidental record of a town’s slow disappearance.

title: The Understudy
author: Nuala Devine
description: She has played the second part for twenty years, and tonight the lead does not arrive.

title: Cold Reading
author: Ilse Brandt
description: A stage mentalist helps with a missing-persons case and finds her tricks work uncomfortably well.

title: Ledger
author: Ilse Brandt
description: A forensic accountant and a former mentalist work the same case from opposite ends.

title: The Second Witness
author: Ilse Brandt
description: Everyone agrees what happened. The one person who disagrees was not there.

title: The Nightjar Papers
author: Yusuf Karim
description: A literary estate, a disputed manuscript, and an archivist who is not who she says she is.

title: A Thin Alibi
author: Gordon Achebe
description: The suspect has an alibi for the murder but not for the eleven minutes before it.

title: The Roscoe Street Fire
author: Gordon Achebe
description: Six flats, one fire, and an insurance investigator who cannot make the timeline close.

title: Dead Reckoning
author: Marta Silvestri
description: A yacht arrives in port with full sails, a set table, and nobody aboard.

title: The Glasshouse Murders
author: Marta Silvestri
description: A botanical garden, a locked conservatory, and a detective allergic to almost everything in it.

title: What the Porter Saw
author: Edwin Croft
description: A college porter has watched forty years of comings and goings, and remembers all of them.

title: The Quiet Part
author: Edwin Croft
description: A podcast reopens a cold case, and the host starts receiving episodes she did not record.

title: Ninety Seconds
author: Rania Haddad
description: The gap in the CCTV is ninety seconds long. Everything happened inside it.

title: The Tenant Below
author: Rania Haddad
description: She hears her own conversations repeated through the floor, a day late.

title: Small Hours
author: Anneke Vos
description: Sixty short poems written between two and four in the morning across a single winter.

title: Nine Bridges
author: Anneke Vos
description: Each poem named for a crossing in the city where Vos grew up.

title: The Salt Book
author: Anneke Vos
description: Poems about preservation: of fish, of grief, of a language with four remaining speakers.

title: Field Notes for the Sleepless
author: Cormac Rea

title: Bell, Book, Weather
author: Cormac Rea

title: Instructions for a Garden
author: Beatriz Oliveira
description: Every poem is phrased as a horticultural instruction. None of them is about gardening.

title: The Blue Hour Almanac
author: Beatriz Oliveira
description: A year of dusks, one poem each, from a window that never changes.

title: Cargo
author: Tunde Falade
description: Poems about what ships carry and what they leave behind on both shores.

title: The Weight Room
author: Tunde Falade
description: Falade turns the vocabulary of strength training into a language for grief.

title: Hymnal for Empty Rooms
author: Saoirse Whelan
description: Sparse, liturgical poems written after the closing of a rural parish.

title: The Weight of Maps

title: The Merchant’s Clock

title: Common Ground
author: Ruth Ó Cadhla

title: Saltpetre
author: Hugh Marchetti

title: The Coffee Ledger
author: Hugh Marchetti

title: Cities Under Cities
author: Anais Perrot

title: The Cartulary
author: Anais Perrot
description: A single monastery’s property records, read as a thousand-year social history.

title: Plague Roads
author: Sunil Mehta
description: The routes disease travelled were the routes trade had already built.

title: The Signal Corps
author: Sunil Mehta
description: Semaphore, telegraph, radio: how command outran the speed of a horse.

title: Empire of Wool
author: Greta Lindqvist
description: Sheep, cloth, and the making of the North Atlantic economy.

title: The Last Ferry

description: Island communities and the infrastructure decisions that quietly ended them.

title: Root and Branch
author: Fern Whitlock

title: Sleep, Interrupted

title: The Attention Economy of the Brain
author: Dr. Naomi Sung

author: Ezra Kohn
description: Reading four billion years out of a single tidal flat.

title: The Isotope Diaries

title: Swarm

title: Antifragile Bones

description: Why bone is a living material, and what engineers keep learning from it.

title: The Silent Spectrum
author: Marcus Oyelaran

title: Weather Machines
author: Clara Dubois

title: The Origin of Salt
author: Clara Dubois

author: Devan Roy

author: Devan Roy

title: The Debugging Mind
author: Devan Roy
description: Not tools but method: how good engineers form and kill hypotheses.

title: Observability Without Tears

title: The Small Web

title: Interface Debt

title: Type Systems for Working Programmers
author: Anders Krogh

title: The Migration

title: Rate Limits
author: Ola Adeyemi

title: Schema Evolution
author: Ola Adeyemi

title: The Instrument Maker

title: Second Chair
author: Lucia Ferrante

title: A Life in Margins

title: The Reluctant Cartographer

title: Hands

title: The Understudied Life
author: Amara Nkemdirim

title: Correspondence
author: Ivan Petrov

title: The Long Apprenticeship

title: Stagehand

title: The Keeper of Records
author: Bridget Ó Muirí
description: A parish registrar whose careful handwriting outlasted every institution she served.

title: The Grid and the Gutter
author: Johannes Weiss
description: Swiss typography’s long argument with itself, told through fifty spreads.

title: Colour Before Chemistry
author: Johannes Weiss
description: Where pigment came from before it came from a factory.

title: Bindings
author: Estelle Faure
description: Six centuries of bookbinding as structural engineering and as argument.

title: The Marginal Hand
author: Estelle Faure
description: Doodles, corrections, and glosses: what readers did to the books they owned.

title: Shop Fronts

description: Vernacular signage from twelve cities, photographed before it disappears.

title: The Chair Problem

title: Everything Is a Poster

title: The Second Draft
author: Kofi Mensah
description: Design process from twenty studios, showing the versions nobody publishes.

title: The Frost Line
author: Ada Fenwick
description: A border town where the boundary moves each winter, and the paperwork never keeps up.

title: Tidal Mathematics
author: Ezra Kohn
description: Predicting the sea: two thousand years of getting it almost right.

title: Systems That Outlive You
author: Kenji Watanabe
description: Writing software on the assumption that someone else will maintain it for a decade.
